episodes.214127: Intense daytime heating combined with near record monsoon moisture under an upper level high centered over west-central NM July 24th, resulting in scattered to numerous thunderstorms across the higher terrain, Rio Grande Valley, and eastern plains during the afternoon and evening hours. Thunderstorms produced debris flows on and downstream of the South Fork burn scar in Ruidoso, flash flooding and thunderstorm wind damage due to wind gusts up to 78 mph in Albuquerque, and flash flooding in the Zuni Pueblo. Thunderstorms tapered off after sunset and during the overnight hours due to the loss of daytime heating. The storm activity on July 24th helped develop a disturbance over the state going into July 25th resulting in another round of thunderstorm development across western and central NM during the afternoon hours. Thunderstorms produced more flash flooding in Zuni Pueblo and a debris flow at Perk Canyon in Ruidoso. Thunderstorms developed over the higher terrain once again during the afternoon hours on July 26th with one thunderstorm producing a 61 mph gust at Sierra Blanca Regional Airport.
episodes.214256: Very strong surface heating along a surface pressure trough generated scattered convection across the extreme southwestern Texas Panhandle on the afternoon of the 24th. An dry sub-cloud layer existed this afternoon with dew point depressions around 40-45 degrees which promoted strong downdraft winds. Within these scattered thunderstorms, a microburst likely occurred in rural Parmer County west of Lazbuddie (Parmer County). Law enforcement in Parmer County relayed significant damage to a dairy farm in the region.
episodes.214311: During the late afternoon of July 24, slow-moving thunderstorms led to localized flooding issues in the Rainbow City, Southside, Wellington, Leesburg, and Pratt City areas. The next afternoon, a decaying mesoscale convective system (MCS) moved through Walker and Jefferson counties, causing minor instances of tree damage.
episodes.214558: A thunderstorm produce wind gusts up to 63 in the Loveland area.
episodes.214559: A thunderstorm produced wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph in northern Jefferson County during the late afternoon on the 24th..
episodes.215263: Localized thermodynamic forcing helped to trigger strong to severe convection. Organized discrete storms tracked northeastward to the Idaho and Montana border. Climatologically high moisture availability supported brief heavy downpours, and decaying storms brought a gusty outflow threat to the Interstate 90 corridor late in the evening.
episodes.215264: Localized thermodynamic forcing helped to trigger strong to severe convection. Effective shear, modest convective available potential energy, and high downdraft convective available potential energy supported organized strong but discrete storms initiating near the Snake River canyon in north-central Idaho tracking northeastward.
episodes.215446: Several clusters of thunderstorms moved across north-central Kansas beginning late evening on July 23 into early on the 24th. Localized amounts of 3-4 inches produced minor flooding.
episodes.215907: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a nearby front across portions of southeast South Carolina in the late afternoon and early evening hours. One storm became strong enough to produce an isolated instance of wind damage in Jasper County.
episodes.216094: An active July monsoon pattern persisted throughout Utah, resulting in continued instances of flash flooding and thunderstorm winds.
episodes.216342: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed along a surface trough in central North Dakota, in a hot and somewhat dry air mass that led to high-based thunderstorms and predominantly a threat of damaging thunderstorm wind gusts. Supercells developed in central North Dakota during the afternoon before combining to become a line of storms that moved through the James River Valley in the evening. The most significant wind damage happened early in the event in the city of Washburn in McLean County. Trees were uprooted with enough force to lift concrete and there was extensive roof damage across the area, including at the Memorial Building, the ambulance bay, and multiple businesses. Significant corn crop damage was reported at a farm in south Washburn. Wind speeds were estimated around 100 mph. Late in the event, the largest hail report occurred, with a report of hail 3 inches in diameter near Forbes in Dickey County.
episodes.216493: A short wave embedded within the flow brough slightly more favorable conditions for more organized thunderstorms to the eastern plains. Some of these storms would go on to produce large hail and severe wind gusts.
episodes.216527: A few disturbances moving through the region combined with sufficient moisture and instability allowed for a few rounds of thunderstorms between the 23rd-25th to Southwest and Central MT. The main hazard with storms was severe wind gusts.
episodes.216813: During the evening hours on the 23rd, a cluster of thunderstorms moving east to northeast across portions of east-central and northwest Kansas produced a 63 mph gust and one inch hail in Logan County.
episodes.216952: A westward moving tropical wave coupled with an inverted trough aloft supported afternoon thunderstorms that produced strong marine wind gusts over Tampa Bay and adjacent waters.
episodes.217056: Supercells developed across northwest MN during the afternoon evening hours and tracked east and southeast mainly along and north of Highway 2 merging into several small MCS clusters. These storms produced large hail to 2 inches and damaging winds.
episodes.217103: A monsoon thunderstorm produced severe wind gusts in Mohave County.
episodes.217174: An upper level disturbance brought a round of strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of Lake Superior.
episodes.217185: The approach of a lower tropospheric inverted trough from the Bahamas and a pre-existing convective cloud line over the Lower Florida Keys led to rapid development of showers and thunderstorms over Key West.  A few gale-force wind gusts were measured.
episodes.217186: A convective cloud line just northwest of the Lower Florida Keys assisted in the development of a long-duration waterspout just north of New Town Key West and Stock Island.
episodes.217188: A waterspout was observed south of Big Pine Key in association with convective showers along a cloud line running along the south side of the Lower Florida Keys.
episodes.217280: A stalled frontal boundary near South Florida led to an unsettled weather pattern in late July.

A severe thunderstorm produced a fifty-one knot wind gust at the Missoula ASOS. The strong winds caused widespread tree damage and power outages across the area. Trees were reported down on United States Highway 12 near mile marker sixteen, creating an obstruction. In Missoula, a large tree fell on Prada Drive, blocking the majority of the road, and tree branches littered driveways and yards. Missoula Electric Cooperative reported that approximately three thousand five hundred members lost power shortly after the storm passed, with significant outages in Huson, the Nine Mile Valley, Seeley Lake, and Potomac.

events.narrative: A mature waterspout was observed by NWS employees and the public north of New Town Key West and Stock Island.  The waterspout was of medium width, initially mostly vertical, with the condensation cloud extending fully from cloud base to the water surface.  A spray ring was clearly visible for over 10 minutes.  The waterspout formed on the east end of a nearly-stationary thunderstorm north of Key West.  The waterspout eventually moved southeast, driven by outflow from the thunderstorm at a speed estimated at 20 knots.  At the end of its lifecycle, the waterspout entered Sunset Marina on Stock Island, causing minor damage to peripheral devices on boats including solar power sheets and deck items.  The condensation funnel dissipated with an extreme tilt of approximately 60 degrees from vertical and was tracked via public video shared on social media by its spray ring.
